item.title: Shenzhou-23 crew prepares for 'space rendezvous' as Shenzhou-24 mission nears launch
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-23
Shenzhou-23 crew prepares for ‘space rendezvous’ as Shenzhou-24 mission nears launch The Shenzhou-23 crew aboard China's space station prepares to welcome the incoming Shenzhou-24 crew. Screenshot from CCTV News The Shenzhou-23 crew aboard China's Space Station is making preparations to welcome the incoming Shenzhou-24 crew while continuing to carry out a range of scientific experiments, CCTV News reported on Sunday. The combination of the Shenzhou-24 spacecraft and its Long March-2F carrier rocket was transferred to the launch area on November 17 and is scheduled for launch at an appropriate time in the coming days, according to a release from the China Manned Space Agency (CMSA). With the mission approaching, the space station is preparing for a special "space rendezvous" as the two crews prepare to meet in orbit. Despite the upcoming crew rotation, the three Shenzhou-23 astronauts remain engaged in their scheduled scientific research. In the field of microgravity physics, they have completed the retrieval of samples from the variable gravity science experiment cabinet, replaced and disposed of samples in the high-temperature materials science experiment cabinet, and replaced components of an inertial particle experiment device in the on-orbit maintenance and assembly operation cabinet. In the field of space technology and applications, the crew has also installed samples for two research projects focusing on microbial prevention and control materials, as well as rapid microbial detection and technical protection. Preparing for the arrival of a new crew involves more than completing scientific tasks. The Shenzhou-23 crew has been cleaning the station's interior and putting its living quarters in order to ensure that the orbital outpost is ready to accommodate the newcomers, per CCTV News. Once the Shenzhou-24 crew arrives, the number of astronauts aboard the space station will increase from three to six for a period of time, significantly raising demand for essential resources such as oxygen and water. To accommodate the additional crew members, the astronauts must adjust settings for the station's operating systems and living facilities in advance. These preparations include configuring lighting in sleeping areas, setting up the urine and feces collection equipment in the space station's toilets, checking the power supply to galley equipment, and adjusting the cabin's environmental control systems to ensure that the facilities can support six astronauts simultaneously. The station's regenerative life support system will play a crucial role in meeting the increased demand. Technologies such as oxygen generation through water electrolysis, carbon dioxide removal and urine processing enable the station to recycle resources and reduce its dependence on supplies delivered from Earth, supporting long-term human presence in orbit. The upcoming crew rotation will also mark a milestone in international space cooperation. A Pakistani astronaut will join the Shenzhou-24 mission as a payload specialist and travel to China's space station, marking the first time that Chinese and foreign astronauts will participate in a joint spaceflight mission under China's manned space program. The visit will also make him the first foreign astronaut to enter the China space station, according to CCTV News. The 'space rendezvous' of the two crews will be followed by a special meal together in orbit. At the same time, the Shenzhou-23 crew is making preparations for its eventual return to Earth. These include collecting cabin gas, microbial and water samples, retrieving experimental samples and payloads to be brought back to Earth, and clearing away waste and personal belongings. According to the mission arrangements, one member of the Shenzhou-23 crew will remain aboard the space station after the crew transition, although the astronaut's identity has not yet been announced, CCTV News reported. The Shenzhou-24 crewed mission has also entered its final preparatory stage. On Saturday, the mission completed its final full-system rehearsal, while the launch site completed preparations for the upcoming launch, as reported by the Xinhua News Agency. item.title: China cuts minimum stock margin requirement to 80%, potentially freeing up 400b yuan in additional funds
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-23
China cuts minimum stock margin requirement to 80%, potentially freeing up 400b yuan in additional funds China's three stock exchanges announced on Sunday that they will cut the minimum requirement for margin financing from 100 percent to 80 percent, effective November 30, a move that could theoretically free up nearly 400 billion yuan ($56 billion) in additional funds, as regulators seek to stabilize the capital market and bolster investor confidence. The adjustment, approved by the China Securities Regulatory Commission, was announced by the Shanghai, Shenzhen and Beijing stock exchanges as part of efforts to strengthen countercyclical regulation and promote the stable development of margin financing and securities lending. For example, under the new rules, investors with 1 million yuan in collateral can borrow up to 1.25 million yuan to purchase securities, compared with 1 million yuan previously, increasing their borrowing capacity by 25 percent, according to the Shanghai Securities News. Wang Peng, an associate research fellow at the Beijing Academy of Social Sciences, told the Global Times that the adjustment sends a positive signal of China's determination to stabilize market expectations and strengthen investor confidence. Against the backdrop of declining margin financing balances and subdued trading activity, easing financing requirements could help improve market liquidity, encourage greater participation and provide investors with more flexibility in managing their capital. The move also highlights the flexibility of China's countercyclical capital market regulation, Wang said. Earlier this year, regulators raised the minimum margin requirement to contain excessive leverage and prevent market overheating. The latest reduction reflects a timely response to changing market conditions, demonstrating policymakers' efforts to balance financial risk prevention with sufficient market liquidity. According to the Shanghai Securities News, the margin financing requirement has been at a historically high level, leaving room for a reduction. Starting in the second half of this year, the stock market has retreated sharply from its highs, with margin financing balances and trading activity declining significantly, while overall leverage has remained relatively low. Outstanding margin financing balances stand at about 2.2 trillion yuan, with available collateral estimated at between 500 billion yuan and 1 trillion yuan. Lowering the minimum requirement to 80 percent could release nearly 100 billion yuan in additional financing capacity, and applying the new requirement to existing financing contracts could free up another 300 billion yuan, according to the report. Wang further noted that the adjustment comes as China continues to deepen capital market reforms, encourage long-term investment and improve the market's capacity to serve the real economy. While additional liquidity could support a recovery in market sentiment, sustainable growth ultimately depends on China's economic fundamentals, the quality of listed companies and continued institutional improvements. Strengthening risk management alongside measures to stimulate market activity will be essential to long-term stability, he said. Broader capital market reforms were announced on Sunday. The Shenzhen Stock Exchange began to solicit public feedback on draft rules to introduce a market making mechanism for stocks on its ChiNext board, an initiative aimed at strengthening market stability, resilience and trading quality, according to the Xinhua News Agency. Meanwhile, the Shanghai and Shenzhen exchanges introduced new fee reductions, including waivers of trading unit usage fees, while extending existing exemptions for listing fees and bond transaction fees by two years through 2028. The China Securities Depository and Clearing Corp Ltd will also extend fee exemptions for certain green, technology innovation and private-sector corporate bonds from January 2027 through December 2028, Xinhua reported. item.title: The world is talking about Shenzhen – what are they talking about?: Global Times editorial
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-23
The world is talking about Shenzhen – what are they talking about?: Global Times editorial APEC China 2026. Illustration: Liu Rui/GT Viewed from the world's perspective, Western developed countries are not only observing where China is headed but also reflecting on what they may have missed. Developing nations are examining what kinds of urban lifestyles and industrial development can become a reality, and whether the path to industrialization must necessarily follow the old path of "polluting first, then cleaning up." Shenzhen is not the sole answer to the future, yet it proves there is more than one path forward. Over the past week, Shenzhen has undoubtedly stood at the center of the world's spotlight. In media reports from around the globe - ranging from its densely packed skyscrapers to self-driving taxis on the streets - Shenzhen has been portrayed as a "futuristic city." Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney praised Shenzhen, saying, "The future is designed here, tested here and built here." US President Donald Trump noted that Shenzhen is "clean" and "immaculate," adding that, in contrast, the development and governance of some US cities are "embarrassing." Peruvian President Keiko Fujimori stated that "there is no doubt that we can learn from Shenzhen" in its approach to smart and digital urban governance. On overseas social media platforms, "Shenzhen" continues to dominate the feed. One netizen wrote, "This might be the most futuristic city I've ever visited in my life," while another added, "I wish my country could have a Shenzhen too." Why has a once remote fishing village attracted so much attention? When the world talks about Shenzhen, what exactly are they talking about? Perhaps the answer lies in one word: future. Seen from within China, Shenzhen embodies the concrete form of Chinese modernization, offering a vivid interpretation of the idea that "the next 'China' is still China." When the Special Economic Zone was established in 1980, Shenzhen's population was less than 30,000. Now, it has developed into a modern international metropolis and "super hub" with a population of over 18 million. Today, people here see self-driving cars cruising the streets, drone deliveries becoming part of daily life, robots operating in factories and shopping malls, and companies like Huawei, BYD, DJI, and Tencent making their mark on the global market. Behind these achievements lie China's sustained investment and stable planning - rooted in its own development and oriented toward the future - and, ultimately, a people-centered approach to development. Viewed from the world's perspective, Western developed countries are not only observing where China is headed but also reflecting on what they may have missed. A key reason why Trump's assessment of Shenzhen's roads and urban environment sparked debate in US public opinion is that it touched on the long-standing challenges of urban governance facing American society. Road maintenance, public transportation, and environmental sanitation - these seemingly ordinary public services are, in fact, persistent challenges that many countries struggle to address. Developing nations, meanwhile, are examining what kinds of urban lifestyles and industrial development can become a reality, and whether the path to industrialization must necessarily follow the old path of "polluting first, then cleaning up." Whether developed or developing, countries are beginning to consider whether they should pursue this kind of future. Shenzhen is not the sole answer to the future, yet it proves that there is more than one path forward. Different countries have different historical traditions, cultural practices, resource endowments, and social systems; there can be no single "standard answer" for urban modernization. Nor is Shenzhen's path a template that can be simply replicated. Its significance lies in demonstrating that openness can spur innovation, industry can foster technology, technology can improve lives, and global cooperation can expand the scope for development. Chilean President Jose Antonio Kast remarked, "Shenzhen's transformation reminds us that progress is not a miracle but a resolution." Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese, drawing on his experiences from visits in 1998 and 2026, remarked that if someone were to place photographs from then and now side by side, it was almost impossible to believe they were of the same place. This demonstrates that the future can be continuously shaped through reform, opening-up, and relentless exploration. What the world needs is not a replica of Shenzhen, but more cities like Shenzhen that can shape their own futures. Today, Shenzhen has evolved from a place where the Chinese people learned about the world through the "window of the world" to a place where the world observes China and envisions the future. In just over 40 years, Shenzhen has traversed a journey that took some major international metropolises abroad more than a century to complete, proving that modernization does not follow a single predetermined path. A late-developing economy can fully forge its own path - one that balances efficiency with people's livelihoods, and vitality with order. This demonstrates that the "future" is not merely a fixed blueprint. Every country and every civilization can draw upon its own historical traditions, social structures, and resource endowments to find a "future blueprint" that suits it best. British urban planning scholar Peter Hall once wrote Cities of Tomorrow, which traces urban planning practices from the late 19th century to the late 20th century - a work in which London, New York, Paris, and Chicago frequently feature. Today, one "city of tomorrow" after another is emerging across China. We welcome more countries, enterprises, research institutions, and innovators to come to Shenzhen. Rather than merely viewing a single "pre-existing model," we can strive to build more models and explore abundant future forms of AI, green development, urban governance, public services, and industrial cooperation. Shenzhen's story is far from finished, and the exploration of Chinese modernization is still underway. The invitation Shenzhen extends to the world is this: China is willing to showcase its own future, and welcomes the world to bring its own dreams here to jointly create even more bright futures. item.title: Shoulder the responsibilities of major countries and safeguard world peace
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-23
Shoulder the responsibilities of major countries and safeguard world peace On Nov. 19, Chinese President Xi Jinping held a China-Russia-U.S. summit with Russian President Vladimir Putin and U.S. President Donald Trump in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong province. The historic trilateral summit marked the first-ever face-to-face meeting between the Chinese, Russian, and U.S. heads of state, making it a groundbreaking event that will go down in history. Following the summit, the three countries released the China-Russia-U.S. Heads of State Declaration toward Peace, expressing their commitment to maintaining strategic stability and international security. Against a backdrop of global turbulence and uncertainty, the summit further underscored the three countries' resolve to uphold dialogue and manage differences. It helped build consensus on maintaining strategic stability among major countries and safeguarding world peace, while sowing the seeds of building consensus through dialogue, taking responsibilities in meeting challenges, and promoting peace through cooperation. Spanning approximately 90 minutes, the summit drew worldwide attention and reflected the international community's strong desire for peace and stability. Today, changes unseen in a century are accelerating across the globe, geopolitical rivalries are intensifying, and localized conflicts are occurring frequently. With humanity sharing a common destiny, positive interaction among major countries is no longer optional -- it is imperative. Whether in global development, food security, energy security, climate governance, public health cooperation, or global artificial intelligence (AI) governance, coordination and cooperation among major countries are indispensable. Conflicts and disputes continue to erupt around the world, with one hotspot flaring up as another subsides. The international community expects major countries to do more to promote reconciliation and peace talks. As major countries and permanent members of the United Nations Security Council, China, Russia, and the U.S. share common interests in strengthening communication, managing differences, and working together to address global challenges. These expectations align closely with broader international sentiment. At the summit, Xi made four points on how major countries could find the right way to get along and jointly underpin world peace, calling for mutual respect, peaceful coexistence, win-win cooperation, and dialogue and consultation. Respect is a fundamental principle in major-country interactions. China, Russia, and the U.S. have different national conditions and should respect one another, seek common ground while reserving differences, and pursue shared development. They should respect one another's sovereignty and territorial integrity, the social systems and development paths of their own choice, and their respective core interests and major concerns, while adhering to the principle of non-interference in other countries' internal affairs. Peaceful coexistence is the bottom line for relations among major countries. China, Russia and the U.S. should be partners and friends. They should not go for conflict or confrontation among them, and avoid falling into the "Thucydides Trap." They should bear in mind that a nuclear war cannot be won and must never be fought, and work together to safeguard the postwar international order and uphold the purposes of the UN Charter. Win-win cooperation is another imperative. China, Russia and the U.S. have different development endowments and strong economic complementarity. They can leverage their respective strengths and reinforce one another with what one has to offer. They should firmly oppose decoupling and disruption of industrial and supply chains, and work together to maintain stable and unimpeded energy industrial and supply chains. The three countries should also remain committed to dialogue and consultation, so as to reduce misjudgments, properly manage differences and prevent frictions from escalating. These four points build on one another, charting a course for major countries to pursue peaceful coexistence and development. Their significance extends far beyond the three countries. China adheres to the path of peaceful development. In recent years, China has been promoting the China-Russia comprehensive strategic partnership of coordination for the new era and actively developing the constructive China-U.S. relationship of strategic stability, with a view to fostering major-country dynamics featuring peaceful coexistence, overall stability and balanced development to the benefit of each other and the world at large. The summit fully demonstrated China's efforts to promote coordination and positive interaction among major countries, as well as its sincerity in managing differences through dialogue and promoting peace and pursuing win-win outcomes through cooperation. "The leaders of these three countries, which are among the most important players on the world stage and are permanent members of the UN Security Council, decided to use the multilateral setting of the APEC summit in Shenzhen to meet face to face, discuss their main concerns, engage in constructive dialogue on issues of common interest, reduce the risk of unintended conflicts arising from strategic miscalculations and curb tensions among the great powers. That in itself is an important diplomatic achievement," said a scholar quoted in an article on the website of Russia's TASS news agency. The U.S. magazine Foreign Affairs observed that the meeting between the three leaders could pave the way for great-power cooperation across ideological lines and stabilize a fragmented world. These international assessments echo China's position and underscore the timeliness and significance of the summit. Viewed from a broad historical perspective, the summit carries even deeper significance for our times. Major countries have always played a uniquely important role in maintaining global strategic stability, safeguarding regional peace, and promoting common development for humanity. Peace among major countries brings stability to the world, while rivalry and confrontation among them can only lead to chaos. More than 80 years ago, China, Russia and the U.S., as key anti-fascist forces in the world, fought shoulder to shoulder and achieved great victories, winning peace and tranquility for the world. The lessons of history remain relevant today: cooperation is the way to jointly withstand risks, while confrontation only breeds disaster. The world today is far from peaceful, with turbulence and conflict intertwined. It is the call of our times and a mission entrusted by history for China, Russia and the U.S. to demonstrate a sense of responsibility, shoulder the responsibilities befitting major countries, and lead and advance multipolarity and greater democracy in international relations. Putin said safeguarding the purposes and principles of the UN Charter and upholding international peace are their shared responsibilities, and they should adhere to the principles of sovereign equality and noninterference in internal affairs, jointly safeguard energy and food security, and strengthen international cooperation on AI governance. Trump said that the summit is a historic event of great importance, drawing global attention. Noting that dialogue is essential to maintaining stability and achieving peace, Trump said all issues should be resolved through dialogue. Some international commentators have simplistically labeled the summit as an example of "great-power condominium" or "Yalta 2.0." Such interpretations essentially apply outdated notions of power politics and the division of spheres of influence to a new form of interaction among major countries in the new era. This misreading ignores both the profound changes in the international landscape and the widespread aspiration of countries around the world to participate in global affairs on an equal footing. The trend toward a multipolar world is irreversible, and bloc confrontation offers no way forward. All parties should take a realistic approach, pave the way for multilateral cooperation, promote common development, and find the right way for major countries to get along in the new era. Only by recognizing this can the true value of the summit be understood: it was not about a "deal" among major countries, but rather a new attempt by them to address differences through dialogue instead of confrontation. As long as all parties work toward the same goal and continue to act on the consensus reached, the seeds sown at the trilateral summit will eventually take root, sprout, bloom, and bear fruit. China stands ready to work with Russia and the U.S. to implement the consensus reached by the three leaders, continue to strengthen communication, meet global challenges, safeguard world peace and stability, and jointly make the world a better place. item.title: Forum on overseas studies of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era held in Uzbekistan
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-23
Forum on overseas studies of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era held in Uzbekistan Participants attend a thematic forum of the 2026 edition of the International Forum on Overseas Studies of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era in Tashkent, capital of Uzbekistan, Nov. 21, 2026. (Xinhua/Zafar Khalilov) TASHKENT, Nov. 22 (Xinhua) -- A thematic forum of the 2026 edition of the International Forum on Overseas Studies of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era was held Saturday in Tashkent, capital of Uzbekistan. Co-organized by the Institute of Russian, Eastern European and Central Asian Studies of the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences and the University of World Economy and Diplomacy of Uzbekistan, the forum was themed "China-Central Asia: High-Quality Belt and Road Cooperation and Green, Innovation-Driven Development." Participants noted that the "Book House for Xi Jinping's Works," which was inaugurated in January this year, serves as an important platform for China and Uzbekistan to deepen research on Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era and exchange experience in state governance. They added that China's innovative proposal of the Belt and Road Initiative helps strengthen policy and strategic coordination among countries. The participants also said the forum's theme has strong practical significance. They stressed that when proposing new infrastructure and technical solutions for Central Asia, all parties should take full consideration of regional characteristics, the actual needs of each country and future development priorities, in which universities, research institutions and think tank experts play an important role. At the seminar, think tank experts and university scholars from China and Central Asian countries conducted in-depth discussions on topics including the Green Silk Road and the pursuit of sustainable development. item.title: China's tech innovation engine powers a connected Asia-Pacific
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-23
China's tech innovation engine powers a connected Asia-Pacific An APEC-themed installation is seen on Xiangmihu road in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province, Nov. 15, 2026. (Xinhua/Jin Liwang) * China's push to unleash the potential of innovation and share technological dividends through open regional integration has resonated widely -- translating its innovation capacity into broader market opportunities and lending fresh momentum to economic growth and the building of an Asia-Pacific community. * Across the Asia-Pacific, China's technological innovations are finding applications in a growing range of industries and aspects of everyday life. * The release of the Shenzhen Initiative marked a milestone in the 30-year history of the APEC CEO Summit. It was a historic moment in Shenzhen, a city that has stood at the forefront of China's opening-up and has grown into a global innovation hub. BEIJING, Nov. 22 (Xinhua) -- As host of the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting in Shenzhen, China has placed openness, innovation and cooperation at the heart of its agenda as the three priority areas. Throughout this week's sessions, participants explored how the Asia-Pacific can navigate structural shifts and cultivate new engines of economic growth. China's push to unleash the potential of innovation and share technological dividends through open regional integration has resonated widely -- translating its innovation capacity into broader market opportunities and lending fresh momentum to economic growth and the building of an Asia-Pacific community. INNOVATION THAT BENEFITS ALL At an experimental durian orchard at Chiang Mai University in Thailand, agricultural lecturer Supakorn Wongsuk prepares a drone for takeoff. Having studied in China, he now applies the technology to explore more efficient methods of cultivating tropical fruits. Lifting smoothly into the air, the drone glides above rows of durian trees, releasing a fine mist of pesticide across their leaves and branches. "Using drones to spray pesticides can improve operational efficiency, reduce farmers' direct exposure to chemicals, and protect their health and safety," said Supakorn. He sees the Chinese innovations as offering benefits that extend well beyond farming efficiency. "For young people, drone operations can also create new job opportunities." Across the Asia-Pacific, China's technological innovations are finding applications in a growing range of industries and aspects of everyday life. The role of innovation also drew sharp focus at the APEC CEO Summit 2026 in Shenzhen. "Innovation is very important, and innovation cannot be done overnight. It requires strong education support and accumulated experience. This is where we think China can play a role," said Indonesian Chamber of Commerce and Industry Chairman Anindya N. Bakrie. "China has an important role to play," said Julien Leclair-Dionne, associate director at the University of Ottawa's Professional Development Institute. "Particularly given its technological capabilities, innovation ecosystem and experience in scaling emerging technologies." An AI trainer operates a robot to collect data at a humanoid robot innovation center in Wuhan, central China's Hubei Province, Nov. 11, 2026. (Xinhua/Wu Zhizun) "Ultimately, what matters most is not simply how advanced the technologies become, but how effectively the innovations are translated into opportunities for people, organizations and communities across the region," he said. OPENNESS CREATES OPPORTUNITIES Released on Wednesday, the Shenzhen Initiative of the APEC CEO Summit 2026 highlighted the transformative potential of frontier technologies such as artificial intelligence, while recognizing the accompanying risks and regulatory challenges that require coordinated regional oversight. At the heart of the document lies a clear, unified conviction among business leaders: no single economy can capture the promise of breakthrough technology -- or tame its disruptions -- alone; only deep regional cooperation can turn innovation into shared prosperity. Auckland Business Chamber CEO Simon Bridges emphasized the need for cooperation amid global uncertainty. "I think cooperation is probably the byword of APEC. And we know in the world right now, it's more important than ever," he said. China's approach to AI development provides "a very good example" that allows others to learn from its technological advances, he added. The appeal of Chinese AI models has become increasingly evident across the region. In South Korea, nearly half of the AI models released by local developers on Hugging Face, a globally popular open-source platform, between January and August this year were based on Chinese foundation models. "China has adopted AI with more open-weight, open-source, low-cost models that are going to be used by businesses around the world," said Jacob Cooke, CEO of WPIC Marketing + Technologies, a leading e-commerce and technology consultancy. "These Chinese companies have done their best to get this technology out to help people," Cooke said at the summit. The opening ceremony of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) CEO Summit 2026 is held in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province, Nov. 18, 2026. (Xinhua/Xie Huanchi) The release of the Shenzhen Initiative marked a milestone in the 30-year history of the APEC CEO Summit. It was a historic moment in Shenzhen, a city that has stood at the forefront of China's opening-up and has grown into a global innovation hub. For Lee Ju-kwan, director of the National Center for APEC Studies at the Korea Institute for International Economic Policy of South Korea, Shenzhen's relentless innovation engine came vividly into focus during a visit to electric vehicle giant BYD's headquarters, offering a firsthand look at the homegrown tech muscle powering the city. "I was deeply impressed by what I saw, particularly robots performing tasks that would traditionally be carried out by human workers on the production line," Lee said. "This year, by hosting APEC, China has taken the opportunity to put forward and renew initiatives aimed at promoting openness and cooperation. I believe these efforts deserve attention and support," Lee said. GREEN INNOVATION "It's the most fantastic ride," said Jeffrey Sachs, a professor at Columbia University, looking back on an epic 15,000-km summer odyssey from Rome to China's Hong Kong, retracing Marco Polo's historic path behind the wheel of a BYD electric vehicle. This photo taken on Sept. 9, 2026 shows an assembly line at the BYD Fuzhou base in Fuzhou, east China's Jiangxi Province. (Xinhua/Wan Xiang) Sachs said the journey showed how far green technology had advanced. "The technology is already here. Most of it is in its most advanced stage in China," Sachs said during a high-level panel at the APEC CEO Summit 2026. He also noted that China had significantly reduced the cost of green technologies, making the transition more affordable. "To go green is not to make an extra burden for the sake of the planet. It's just to have a low-cost, resilient, state-of-the-art energy system," he said. The benefits of China's green innovation are also being felt by residents of Goulburn in New South Wales, Australia. With an integrated solar-and-storage solution supplied by a Chinese company, the local community has brought its own solar farm into operation. The facility began supplying electricity to the grid in March, with part of its annual profits to be channeled into a community fund to help residents facing energy poverty. "For a long time, it has been talk around the kitchen table. Suddenly here we are in amongst the panels, watching the sun send electrons to the people and my kids all own little parts of this with the community," said Goulburn resident Dave Suttle. "Without China's involvement, we definitely wouldn't have solar cells as cheap as now," Martin Green, Scientia Professor of Photovoltaic and Renewable Energy Engineering at the University of New South Wales, told Xinhua. Having worked with China's photovoltaic industry for more than four decades, Green is now collaborating with Chinese partners on the next generation of solar technology. "Working with China, we feel we're in a position to improve the solar performance more quickly," he said. Copyright © 2026 People's Daily Online. All Rights Reserved.

item.title: China's second homegrown large cruise ship begins maiden commercial voyage
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-23
China's second homegrown large cruise ship begins maiden commercial voyage A tourist interacts with a robot on Adora Flora City, China's second domestically built large cruise ship, on Nov. 22, 2026. Adora Flora City embarked on its maiden voyage on Sunday, marking a new step in the country's efforts to expand cruise tourism and boost consumption. (Xinhua) GUANGZHOU, Nov. 22 (Xinhua) -- China's second domestically built large cruise ship, Adora Flora City, embarked on its maiden voyage on Sunday, marking a new step in the country's efforts to expand cruise tourism and boost consumption. Carrying more than 3,800 passengers, the ship departed from Guangzhou in south China's Guangdong Province on a six-day, five-night journey to Hong Kong and Hue, Vietnam. Measuring 341 meters in length and with a gross tonnage of 141,900, the vessel has 2,130 cabins and can accommodate up to 5,232 passengers. Construction of Adora Flora City began in August 2022. Operated by Adora Cruises under China Tourism Group, the ship was delivered in Shanghai, east China, on Nov. 6 and embarked on its first trial voyage on Nov. 9. Shi Dai, chairperson of China Tourism Group, said the company is using cruise operations to drive the development of integrated cultural tourism products and travel experiences, aiming to set a new benchmark for vacations at sea. Adora Flora City is larger and features a more streamlined design than its sister ship, Adora Magic City, China's first domestically built large cruise ship. Adora Magic City began commercial operations in January 2024 and has since completed about 250 voyages. Hu Zhenyu, deputy director of the Qianhai branch of the China Development Institute, said the entry into service of two domestically built large cruise ships marks a new phase for China's cruise industry. The development will not only expand the range of high-quality marine tourism products but also create new drivers of consumption in coastal areas, Hu said. In 2027, Adora Flora City is scheduled to undertake over 50 international voyages from its home port in Guangzhou, offering both short getaways and longer itineraries to destinations including Vietnam, Malaysia and Brunei. The ship will also offer voyages with no scheduled port calls, allowing passengers to enjoy the cruise ship as a destination in itself. The vessel departed from the Guangzhou Nansha International Cruise Home Port, one of China's largest integrated cruise port complexes. A duty-free store at the terminal also opened on Sunday, adding a fresh shopping option for cruise passengers. Wu Qingsong, deputy director of Guangzhou's culture, radio, television and tourism bureau, said the maiden voyage presents an opportunity for the city to better integrate its cruise port, shipping industry and tourism resources. Guo Jia, assistant vice president of product and guest experience at Adora Cruises, said the company plans to expand year-round operations across multiple home ports in east and north China, and the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area, offering passengers more high-quality cruise experiences. The maiden voyage comes as China seeks to expand tourism consumption. A 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-2030) for cultural and tourism development calls for boosting spending on cruise and yacht tours, among other specialized tourism offerings. China has seen strong growth in cruise tourism, with total cruise passenger throughput rising 25.3 percent year on year in 2025, according to the Ministry of Natural Resources. item.title: Xi Story: Bringing Hainan's rainforest back to life
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-23
Xi Story: Bringing Hainan's rainforest back to life HAIKOU, Nov. 22 (Xinhua) -- Zhou Zhaoli, a member of the Hainan gibbon monitoring team, starts his day at 4:30 a.m., long before sunrise. With flashlights in hand, he and his teammates pick their way through dense undergrowth in the mountainous Bawangling area of south China's Hainan Province, braving thorns and leech bites. Their reward is sometimes the sight of Hainan gibbons high in the forest canopy, and the sound of their distinctive calls echoing through the trees at first light. The world's 20 gibbon species live in 11 Asian countries, and most are in decline. Native to the island province's tropical rainforests, the Hainan gibbon was once pushed to the brink of extinction by commercial logging, deforestation and poaching. Today it is the only gibbon species in the world whose population has kept growing. During an inspection tour of Hainan in April 2022, Chinese President Xi Jinping visited part of these rainforests and asked local villagers whether they had seen the rare primates. At that time, the habitat hosted 36 gibbons in five groups. By the end of 2025, the figure reached 44 gibbons in seven groups, up from fewer than 10 in two groups in the early 1980s. Hainan's tropical rainforest is China's largest, best-preserved and most concentrated stretch of contiguous island-type tropical rainforest. The rainforest was once fragmented across more than 20 nature reserves and other protected areas in nine cities and counties. In 2019, Hainan began piloting an integrated approach, placing previously separate nature reserves, forest parks and state-owned forest farms under unified management. About two years later, the Hainan Tropical Rainforest National Park was established as one of China's first five national parks, which together span ecosystems from giant panda habitats in Sichuan, Gansu and Shaanxi provinces to the only home of the Hainan gibbon. Xi has closely followed the park's development. In 2018, he called for establishing national parks, including those protecting tropical rainforests. In 2019, he chaired a key reform meeting that approved a pilot plan for the Hainan national park. In 2021, he announced the establishment of China's first five national parks at the COP15 leaders' summit. During that 2022 inspection tour, Xi walked along a boardwalk in the national park, taking a close look at its natural environment. "He slowed his pace, studying the trees and listening closely to the sounds of nature as we walked," said Zheng Yan, a member of the park's public education and outreach team, who accompanied Xi and introduced the park to him during the visit. The park has improved markedly in both infrastructure and management capacity since its establishment, said Zheng, who has worked there for more than a decade. Xi's interest in rainforest conservation extends beyond China. On a visit to Brazil in July 2014, he recalled his 2009 trip to Manaus, a city deep in the Amazon rainforest, saying that protecting this vast expanse of pristine forest was vital to the global ecosystem. Protecting tropical rainforests is closely tied to humanity's survival and well-being, and it is a shared responsibility that calls for concerted global efforts. In recent years, China and Brazil have deepened cooperation on climate change and sustainable development. With support from the international community, the two countries are exploring new approaches to rainforest conservation and development, including measures that help local farmers improve their livelihoods and reduce deforestation while safeguarding the world's precious ecological assets and advancing global climate goals. Greice Quele Aparecida Barboza de Oliveira, an environmental analyst with Brazil's Chico Mendes Institute for Biodiversity Conservation, visited Hainan recently to learn about China's approach to biodiversity conservation and to see how the national park protects the rare primate. "These are areas I knew little about before. I am studying them closely so that I can take China's experience in wildlife conservation home with me," she said. She was in Hainan for the 2026 Tropical Rainforest Ecosystem Partners Conference, which ended on Sunday and drew international officials, experts and representatives from more than 20 countries. Climate change is becoming an increasingly serious challenge in Brazil and around the world, she said, adding that international cooperation and exchanges like those at the Hainan conference can help share effective conservation practices with other countries. During his 2022 visit to Hainan, Xi also asked about forest rangers' income and village-level public spending. He stressed the need to strictly protect tropical rainforests while ensuring that ecological conservation, green development and improvements in people's livelihoods go hand in hand. Hainan's tropical rainforest lies in one of the world's 34 biodiversity hotspots and serves as a reservoir of water, a source of food and wealth and a carbon sink. "Hainan's tropical rainforest does not belong to Hainan alone. It belongs to the people of the whole country and to Mother Earth as a whole. It is a national treasure," Xi said.
